To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Swedish pensioners’ organizations are important actors for welfare policy development, especially in the area of pensions.
pensioner’ associations have had an influential role in the Swedish welfare state policy development, especially in the 1990s.
pensioners' organizations have been influential on several issues that are of great importance for the elderly, such as the pension system and health care, from the early 1900s to the current time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a controversy in the political science literature about the power of client groups.
the question of whether pensioner organizations have become more influential over time in Sweden.
a controversy in the new politics of welfare literature, which has questioned the importance of client interests for the understanding of retrenchment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

client interests, in this case pensioners' organizations have been influential on the development of pension policy in Sweden, although their influence is not absolute and is not necessarily always positive for pensioners.
the position of pensioners’ organizations in Sweden's welfare state is one where they are both insiders and influential.
the power held by pensioners' organizations is not a result of a shift to new politics, nor of a shift to corporatism, but of a combination of the two.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pensioners’ organizations in Sweden have been able to influence policy development in the area of pensions, even in an institutional setting characterized by corporatism and strong trade unions.
the power of client interests is a matter of the extent and quality of their organization, not a general feature of the policy process in a specific political system.
the Swedish pensioners’ organizations, from being outsiders, have become influential insiders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the influence of client groups in the policy process is not necessarily a result of their position outside the policy process.
pensioners' organizations are an important part of the corporatist system of interest representation in Sweden, and their influence should be considered in future research on the policy process.
pensioner’ groups are important actors for understanding welfare policy development.
